chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Be more hopeful in that for which you have no hope than in that for which you have hope.
For indeed Musa (peace be upon him) went to obtain fire for his family, but he returned to them while he was a commissioned Prophet.

key_terms.أَرْجَى: More hopeful — comparative form of rajā' (hope/expectation); the teaching urges an inversion of ordinary human expectation
key_terms.لِيَقْتَبِسَ: To kindle/obtain fire — from the root q-b-s meaning to take a spark from a fire, indicating a mundane, practical errand
key_terms.نَبِيٌّ مُرْسَلٌ: A commissioned prophet — the dual title emphasizes both prophethood (receiving revelation) and the specific mission of being sent to a people

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about hope in the unexpected in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches a profound lesson in trust and reliance on God: one should place greater hope in the unexpected than in what seems certain. He illustrates this with the story of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him), who set out on a mundane errand — to bring fire for his family on a cold night — yet returned transformed as a commissioned Prophet and Messenger. This teaching was directed at believers facing hardship, reminding them that divine providence operates beyond human calculation.
